findings.text: s71's Deliverable asks for two endpoints: "A run with a delivery hold is not resumed by the station" and "A promotion that finds its pointer changed by a launch made since it began finishes its cleanup against the current attempt when that attempt has ended, and otherwise refuses naming that attempt and the process that launched it"; its Done-when adds three cases, the first proving the hold guard and the second and third proving the promotion cleanup, over two distinct write-path modules (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py` and `reckon/crew/promotion.py`), so one gate verdict covers neither mechanism alone and a repair to one can close the node while the other stays broken

findings.reason: the author must name the observable that distinguishes a held-but-not-resumed run from an inert pass and add the unheld arm that the pass does resume, which changes the case the node builds.
findings.text: the first case "holds a delivered run and asserts the station's repair pass does not resume it", but the section names no observable that the repair pass reacts to: no launch record, no return value and no launch attempt counted, and no arm with the same delivered run without the hold that the pass does resume; a pass that never resumes anything — wrong eligibility, wrong arguments, an exception swallowed earlier — satisfies the assertion, so the case cannot show the refusal happens rather than that the pass is inert, and a `delivery_hold` read that starts refusing every resume also passes it

findings.reason: s71's first clause turns on a held run being resumed, so the author must cite the record that shows the hold (the pointer as read at 21:52Z, or the transcript that wrote it) or restate the Why so the node does not build a guard against a state the incident may never have held.
findings.text: the Why's clause "While the run was held, the station had resumed it itself" rests on run `r-20261115T184907801020-an-answer-the-tick-reads-is-never-evicted` being held at 21:52Z, and the run's own records carry no hold to open: `delivery_hold` is a pointer field (`reckon/crew/resume.py:41`, read only through `resume.delivery_hold`/`hold_reason`), the pointer was removed by the discard, and the surviving artifacts (`attempt-4.reservation`, `attempt-4-exit.json`, `promotion.json`, `landing.json`, `discard.json`) record no hold entry — the nearest surviving fact, the acceptance receipt's `"phase": "promotion-deferred"` at 21:54:32Z, states only that a promotion was deferred, not that a hold was in force
